Oct 21 : US President Donald Trump said if companies want to make data centers popular, they should pay the community or individuals within the community a "dividend".  "I have watched the process closely, and data centers that were highly unpopular in a certain area, have become extremely popular when a financial deal is struck," Trump said in his Truth Social post on Wednesday.  Data centers fueling the rise of AI have become a political flashpoint in communities across the country, with opposition uniting voters across ideological lines.

HONG KONG: Finance ministers from member economies in the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) forum have agreed to strengthen macroeconomic policy communication and coordination to address external risks and challenges, Chinese Minister of Finance Lan Foan said on Wednesday (Oct 21). At the conclusion of the ministers' meeting in Hong Kong, they also reached a consensus on promoting practical cooperation in the financial sector, which focused on supporting people's livelihoods, digital infrastructure financing and locally adapted measures for inclusive finance development, Lan said at a briefing. Separately, a policy statement was released on digital infrastructure financing for the Asia-Pacific region, aimed at supporting regional trade, economic connectivity and enhancing economic opportunities. "We encourage member economies to develop reliable, accessible, scalable, trusted, secure and resilient digital infrastructure; enhance digital literacy and skills; promote interoperability; and cross-border digital connectivity to accelerate the digital transformation in the Asia-Pacific region," it said. Ministers also sought deeper collaboration between the public sector, the private sector and multilateral development banks to foster innovation and risk mitigation, it said.

TOKYO, Oct 21 : Japan's underlying inflation is quite close to the central bank's 2 per cent target and financial conditions remain loose, Deputy Bank of Japan Governor Ryozo Himino said on Wednesday, signalling readiness to raise borrowing costs. While rising fuel and raw material costs are pushing up prices, brisk global AI demand is also putting upward pressure on prices by boosting exports and capital expenditure, Himino told parliament. "Given medium- and long-term inflation expectations continue to heighten, underlying inflation is quite close to 2 per cent and will likely converge to levels consistent with our price target," Himino said. "Even after last month's rate hike, financial conditions remain accommodative" as seen in still-low real borrowing costs and strong growth in bank lending, he said. "Given that inflation risks are high, delaying necessary adjustment to monetary support could materialise such risks and hurt the economy in the long run," Himino said, calling for the need to continue raising interest rates.

Source: Reuters

Oct 21 : State Bank of India on Wednesday reported a cyberattack that resulted in the disclosure of 3,897 customer records containing personally identifiable information on the dark web. SBI said a preliminary analysis showed that the exposed information included customer names, mobile numbers, dates of birth, email addresses, residential addresses, brand and customer identifiers, along with loan records. The lender said it has engaged an independent cybersecurity agency to conduct a comprehensive assessment and investigate the nature and extent of the data leak. The leak is not expected to have any material impact on the bank's core business operations, financial performance or business continuity, the lender said. The incident comes amid heightened regulatory focus, with India's banking regulator pushing lenders to strengthen cybersecurity frameworks in recent years amid a rise in threats targeting financial institutions.

Source: Reuters

Oct 20 : OpenAI said on Tuesday that two of its AI agents weakened parts of an internal monitoring system designed to detect misbehavior, the latest case of AI agents acting in ways their developers did not intend them to. While the ChatGPT maker said the incidents happened during internal coding tasks and were not deemed its most severe, the disclosure highlights even the systems developers rely on to catch AI misbehavior are vulnerable to the agents they monitor. The disclosure also comes amid growing concerns that AI safety efforts are lagging behind the rapid development of increasingly powerful systems. Researchers have warned that advanced AI agents could become harder to monitor and control as they gain greater autonomy. Developers, including IPO-bound rivals OpenAI and Anthropic, have revealed in recent months instances of their AI agents accessing external systems without authorization.

OpenAI said On Tuesday a GPT-6.1 Sol agent working on an internal testing task on October 3 suppressed automatic security alerts after deciding an earlier instruction not to send Slack messages also covered safety notifications. In a separate incident on October 6, a GPT-6 Astra agent removed a safety monitor while copying an existing piece of code and later incorrectly claimed it had not done so, OpenAI said. "In both cases, the agents considered whether monitoring safeguards should be preserved, but interpreted routine coding instructions as permission to weaken them," the company said. OpenAI said it was making it harder for models to disable monitoring, adding that it does not "yet have a satisfying explanation for this behavior". The San Francisco-based company said it was testing whether its models might have a tendency to avoid being monitored and look for reasons to justify doing so.

Source: Reuters

TOKYO, Oct 21 : The US dollar hovered near a three-week low on Wednesday as traders assessed developments in the Middle East after the conflict burnished the currency's appeal as a safe haven amid oil-driven inflation worries. The Australian dollar reached a three-week high against the greenback. Reserve Bank of Australia Deputy Governor Andrew Hauser said at a Citi conference that the inflation outlook looked "materially worse." The Aussie dollar rose 0.2 per cent to $0.70155 at 0525 GMT, after earlier touching $0.70289 for the first time since September 29. The US dollar index, which measures the currency against six peers, was steady at 101.79 after declining 0.2 per cent on Tuesday and dipping as low as 101.50 for the first time since October 1.

Investors have turned to the greenback amid market volatility brought about by the US-Israeli war on Iran, partly due to US energy independence. Oil prices edged toward a five-month high as traders weighed an Iranian media report that Tehran told Pakistan's army chief there would be no talks with Washington until its demands were met. There was no official confirmation of the report. The dollar has also been under pressure with Treasury yields sliding this month, while demand for safe-haven assets has diminished, with Wall Street posting a solid session overnight as technology earnings season got underway with SpaceX results. Japan's Nikkei and South Korea's KOSPI rallied on Wednesday. "With equity market sentiment and the growth outlook closely tied to the performance of the major tech firms, their earnings results can have a large bearing on the USD," said Carol Kong, economist and currency strategist at Commonwealth Bank of Australia, in a client note. Amid a "mixed" performance among traditional haven assets this year, "the USD has been the clear standout," she said. "Safe haven demand for the USD is likely to fade once the Middle East conflict ends and energy prices retreat. However, we expect the USD to trend modestly higher in coming months as foreign capital inflows into US markets increase." The greenback was flat at 158.16 yen, though it edged up to $1.1224 per euro and $1.33735 against sterling. Traders remained wary of the euro as France tackles widespread anti-government protests and a worsening fiscal picture. France will reinforce police with troops and mount a huge security operation for more protests planned on Saturday, the government said on Tuesday, acknowledging failures in its response to violence last weekend. Among central banks, the US Federal Reserve, European Central Bank and Bank of Japan will unveil policy decisions on consecutive days starting next Wednesday. Traders do not expect changes in interest rates at any of those meetings. The Reserve Bank of New Zealand and Bank of Canada decide policy on the same day as the Fed, with traders betting on quarter-point hikes by both. The New Zealand dollar slipped 0.2 per cent to $0.5675 on Wednesday, while Canada's loonie was steady at C$1.4064.

Source: Reuters

SYDNEY, Oct 21 : Australian data centre operator NextDC shed nearly half of its market value on Wednesday after sharply cutting revenue forecasts for the year ahead and putting future developments on hold. The company said delays to electricity network upgrades at one of its major Melbourne projects would mean about A$140 million ($98 million) worth of contracted customer revenue this financial year would be deferred. NextDC said it would shelve all new development projects and land acquisitions for the foreseeable future and would evaluate capital recycling opportunities, including potential sales of selected development sites. NextDC shares closed down 41.7 per cent with about A$3 billion wiped from its market value in its worst day of trade since listing in 2010. The stock was also the biggest loser on the broader ASX200 benchmark index, which closed up 0.16 per cent.

AI exuberance has given way to caution, dragging down data centre and technology stocks as investors reassess growth expectations and the sector's rich valuations. Sentiment towards the new technology has weakened in recent weeks as investors question whether massive AI spending can justify soaring computing, land and power costs. Signs of strain are emerging in some of those bets, with a data centre IPO withdrawn in Australia last week and credit investors becoming increasingly selective toward AI-linked companies. Shares in South Korean AI firm Elice rebounded 30 per cent on Wednesday after falling 32 per cent on the stock's first day of trade on Tuesday. The debut was the worst ever in Seoul for a company's IPO that raised more than $100 million. NextDC now expects net revenue of A$475 million to A$500 million in 2027, down from its prior outlook of A$615 million to A$640 million, excluding the affected M3 contracts. The company also cut its 2027 underlying earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortisation (EBITDA) forecast to A$245 million to A$265 million, from A$385 million to A$410 million, excluding the affected M3 contracts. Delays to works by Jemena Electricity Networks meant the next increase in supply to its M3 Melbourne data centre was now expected in 2028, NextDC said. The site is also facing delayed approval times for its expansion plans due to an election being held in the state of Victoria on November 28. "Together with later grid supply, this delays M3's final capacity stages by several years," said Macquarie analysts, who added NextDC had limited other choices to secure power. Jemena had suspended parts of the electricity network works needed to increase power supply to M3 due to opposition from the community and stakeholders and does not expect to recommence them before February 2027. "Whilst out of the company's control, delays to power supply and development applications relating to NXT's M3 data centre is evidence that community concerns around data centre developments present a real risk to the timing of delivery of contracted capacity for data centre owners," said Tom Beadle, an RBC Capital Markets analyst. Separately, NextDC lowered its 2027 capital expenditure outlook to A$4.5 billion to A$5 billion from A$5.25 billion to A$5.75 billion and said it had begun a detailed review of its spending programme. NextDC said it would release the initial results of that review at its annual investor meeting on November 20. ($1 = 1.4271 Australian dollars)

BEIJING, Oct 21 : Oil prices gained over $1 on Wednesday as escalating Middle East tensions fuelled fears of supply disruptions, while falling US crude and product inventories lent support to the market. Brent crude futures rose $1.59, or 1.5 per cent, to $110.38 per barrel as of 0350 GMT. US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude gained $1.36, or 1.4 per cent, to $99.18 per barrel. Prices fell in the previous trading session after Iran's president discussed mediation efforts in a meeting with Pakistan's army chief in Tehran, though Brent hit a five-month high before easing. "Oil prices have been having a bit of wild ride in the last couple of sessions," said Suvro Sarkar, head of energy research at DBS.

Iran told Pakistan's army chief there would be no talks with Washington until its demands were met, Iranian media outlet Nournews reported on Tuesday, adding that a Qatari delegation had arrived in Tehran. There was no official confirmation of the reports. Maritime security risks are also escalating. Shiptracker Kpler said on Monday that at least 18 vessel attacks were recorded over the past two weeks, while LSEG analysts warned Iran was targeting tankers well beyond the Strait of Hormuz, reaching into the Gulf of Oman and jeopardising Gulf crude loadings and the ship-to-ship transfers supporting regional loadings. In Saudi Arabia, the Houthis on Monday claimed responsibility for attacks on a Saudi Aramco site in Yanbu, the Shaybah oilfield and Saudi Arabia's Riyadh and Abha airports. The death toll from a Houthi attack on Yemeni government forces on Monday rose to 73 as fighting intensified. Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi said in a television interview aired on Tuesday that Iran has not received a response from Saudi Arabia or Yemen's Houthis to its offer to help broker peace talks. In the US, two Energy Department officials said on Tuesday they were working with refiners around the world to boost fuel output as a diesel shortage has raised prices. According to market sources citing API data, US crude stocks fell by 4.9 million barrels in the week ended October 16.

Source: Reuters

SEOUL, Oct 21 : South Korea's exports surged 105.4 per cent in the first 20 days of this month from a year earlier, led by record chip sales driven by global AI investment, customs data showed on Wednesday. On a working-day average basis, exports were up 65.9 per cent at a record $4.74 billion. Exports of semiconductors rose 222.5 per cent, accounting for 44.7 per cent of the total. Last month, exports rose 83.7 per cent, the biggest jump since February 1974, with the monthly value topping $120 billion for the first time.

TOKYO, Oct 21 : Japanese exports in September rose 16.7 per cent year-on-year, up for a 13th straight month, data from the Ministry of Finance showed on Wednesday. The result compared with a 20.1 per cent increase expected by economists in a Reuters poll. Imports grew 18.9 per cent in September from a year earlier, versus a 19.6 per cent increase expected by economists. As a result, the trade balance stood at a deficit of 536.6 billion yen ($3.39 billion), compared with a forecast deficit of 181 billion yen. ($1 = 158.2600 yen)

LOS ANGELES, Oct 20 : AI data center construction projects, particularly near Dallas/Fort Worth and Washington, DC, are generating new demand for warehouse space and helped send rents higher in the third quarter, real estate services company JLL said on Tuesday. • Companies like Alphabet, Microsoft, Meta and Amazon are spending billions of dollars in a race to dominate artificial intelligence, which requires significant electricity to run servers and computer chips that must be cooled to prevent overheating. • "Data center expansion is driving outsized industrial demand in major freight hubs such as Dallas/Fort Worth, where suppliers and infrastructure providers are clustering near hyperscale campuses," JLL said in its industrial real estate market report for the third quarter. • Average asking rents rose to $10.55 per square foot, up 3.2 per cent from a year earlier, the fastest annual pace of growth since the second quarter of 2024, JLL said.

FAST

TOKYO, Oct 21 : The Bank of Japan will raise interest rates in December to 1.50 per cent, following June and September increases, according to a majority of economists in a Reuters poll, keeping up a quicker pace in a campaign that started with just one rate rise a year. Rising energy and import costs, worsened by a weak yen and the war in the Middle East, are adding to inflation pressure in Japan, and there are more forecasters expecting at least two more rate rises to 2.0 per cent by the middle of next year. A period of relative stability in the yen, which spent most of the year under crushing selling pressure, triggering interventions from the Japanese authorities as well as the US Treasury, also supports the case for a December increase. Last week, board member Junko Koeda said the central bank should not become overly cautious about raising rates, at their highest in 31 years, given the significant upside risks to inflation.

Nearly 70 per cent of economists, 54 of 78, in the October 13-19 survey expected the BOJ to raise its policy rate to 1.5 per cent this quarter, almost double the share in the previous poll. Of the 54 respondents who specified a month, about 80 per cent chose December, while only 2 per cent chose the BOJ's next two-day policy meeting, which concludes on October 30. "With rate hikes in the United States and Europe looking likely before year-end, there is a risk that yen selling could accelerate if the BOJ postpones its move until the new year," said Kazutaka Maeda, senior economist at Meiji Yasuda Research Institute. The BOJ is unlikely to raise rates this month, while the US Federal Reserve and the European Central Bank are expected to raise borrowing costs in December, separate Reuters polls found. "The economy is not overheating to the extent that would warrant consecutive rate hikes, and price developments are also within the BOJ's expected range," said Takeshi Minami, chief economist at Norinchukin Research Institute. Sources have told Reuters many BOJ officials prefer to assess more data on how previous increases have affected financial conditions. RATES TO REACH 2 per cent OR HIGHER Looking into next year, 39 of 65 analysts, or 60 per cent, expected the policy rate to reach 1.75 per cent by end-June, a median unchanged from the September poll. Almost half of 41 respondents who answered an additional question said 1.75 per cent would be the terminal rate. But the share expecting it to reach 2.00 per cent or more rose to 51 per cent, from 40 per cent in September and 36 per cent in August. In September, two board members nominated by Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi who support looser fiscal policy opposed the decision to raise rates to 1.25 per cent.  Traders saw the dissent as a sign the BOJ's rate-hike plans could continue to face opposition from Takaichi's administration, briefly pushing the yen lower. Nearly three-quarters of respondents, or 23 of 32, said further dissenting votes when the Policy Board next raises rates could weigh on the yen, which is only about 4 per cent stronger than its 2026 low of around 164 per dollar. "If the dissenting vote were cast in particular by a board member appointed under the Takaichi administration, it could be interpreted as the administration's attempt to restrain rate hikes, potentially heightening concerns that future policy tightening could fall behind the curve," said Kei Fujimoto, senior economist at Sumitomo Mitsui Trust Asset Management. BOND ISSUANCE SEEN BELOW 40 TRILLION YEN Japanese government bond (JGB) yields have risen recently alongside a global market rout, but also on expectations of further BOJ rate hikes and concerns Takaichi's big spending and tax-cut plans will worsen the country's already strained finances. Takaichi has said the government aims to keep new bond issuance at around 40 trillion yen ($251 billion) for the fiscal 2027 budget. She reiterated on Monday Tokyo would "appropriately" control the size of its debt issuance. Nearly two-thirds of economists surveyed, 15 of 23, said new issuance would be kept below 40 trillion yen. "The government is likely keen to increase JGB issuance as a source of funding for growth investment," said Junya Takemoto, senior economist at Sumitomo Mitsui Banking Corporation.  "However, as it becomes more conscious of rising interest rates in the market, it may seek to contain issuance by undertaking a full-scale review of budgets for existing subsidies and funds, ensuring that JGB issuance does not differ markedly from historical levels." (Other stories from the Reuters global economic poll)

Source: Reuters

Oct 20 : Super Micro Computer expects quarterly revenue and profit margin well above Wall Street estimates as it benefits from relentless AI data center demand, the server maker said on Tuesday, sending shares 11.3 per cent higher in after-hours trading. Rivals Dell and HPE gained between 3.5 per cent and 4.9 per cent. Nvidia, the AI chip giant, was up 1.5 per cent. Big Tech's race to build out data centers has placed firms such as Super Micro among the biggest beneficiaries of the AI boom. Microsoft, Google, Amazon and Meta are expected to spend more than $700 billion on AI infrastructure this year. That is showing up in Super Micro's results.

FORECAST FOLLOWS AI SELLOFF Shares of companies exposed to the AI data-center buildout fell last week after CoreWeave’s stock and bond slide and prospects of higher interest rates triggered concerns that heavily indebted operators could take longer than expected to generate returns. S&P Global said on Monday it estimates the world's biggest tech firms are likely to have more AI-linked liabilities than known. Super Micro on Tuesday said it expects revenue between $18.5 billion and $19.5 billion in the first quarter, compared with analysts’ average estimate of $15.23 billion, according to data compiled by LSEG. That expectation is also well above the company’s prior revenue forecast of $14.5 billion to $15.5 billion. The server maker also now expects gross margins to be in the range of 12 per cent to 12.5 per cent versus the prior expectation of 10.4 per cent to 10.8 per cent, and above analysts' estimate of 10.15 per cent, primarily due to customer and product mix. Super Micro last week appointed former Western Digital executive Mark Long as its chief financial officer, nearly two years after beginning its search amid scrutiny of its financial and accounting practices.

Source: Reuters
